blocks.text: TradeHQ is a small independent project rather than a company with a support desk, so messages are read and answered by the person who builds the site. In practice that means response times vary with request volume and can take longer over a weekend or a public holiday. Nothing is auto-responded to by TradeHQ. You can open an email draft or copy it into webmail. Where configured, a separate direct-send option delivers a validated message through Cloudflare and an email provider to the maintainer; the app does not retain it in its own database.

blocks.text: Bug reports are the most useful thing you can send. If something behaved unexpectedly, include the page address you were on, the browser and device you were using, what you expected to happen and what actually happened. A screenshot removes most of the guesswork. For a problem with a simulated trade, mention the ticker and roughly when it happened. Guest positions are browser-held; signed-in cash and open positions may also be stored by account sync when that service is available. Do not send passwords or private financial records.

blocks.text: Guest practice records are stored in the browser that created them. Optional account sync stores account cash, positions and server-recorded trades for restoration on another device when the service is available. Earlier guest trade history and journal entries remain browser-held. Guest lesson progress and badges are saved in the browser; signed-in lesson completion, unfinished quiz answers, reading position and first-trade journey progress can also be synced privately between devices when online. Clearing browser data removes the local copy, but does not delete a saved account record. Daily streaks and private journals are not included in the learning sync, and portfolio backups do not restore lessons.
